security_audit.summary: Most static findings are documentation syntax, localhost references, or an intentionally unsafe network example and are false positives. Two file-write examples create genuine risks when exporting production histories, including unrestricted destinations and workflow identifiers used in filenames. No prompt injection attempt was found.

remediation.issue: Production history export accepts an unrestricted output path.
remediation.suggestion: Resolve exports beneath a dedicated directory, reject traversal, create files exclusively, and document trusted caller requirements.

remediation.issue: Automated exports place workflow identifiers directly into filenames.
remediation.suggestion: Encode or replace unsafe identifier characters, verify the resolved path remains inside the export directory, and handle collisions.

remediation.issue: Production histories are copied into local and CI environments without data protection guidance.
remediation.suggestion: Document redaction, encryption, retention, access controls, and artifact restrictions for histories containing sensitive payloads.

content.user_title: Test Temporal Python Workflows with Pytest
content.value_statement: Temporal workflow tests can be slow and miss determinism failures. This skill provides focused pytest patterns for time-skipping, mocks, replay, and local setup.
actual_capabilities: Explains time-skipping tests with Temporal WorkflowEnvironment.
Shows activity tests with ActivityEnvironment and pytest.
Provides integration patterns for mocked activities, failures, signals, and queries.
Demonstrates workflow history replay and determinism checks.
Outlines local Docker Compose, coverage, and CI test setup.
limitations: Examples require adaptation to your workflow types, activities, and task queues.
The skill does not provide an executable sample project or run tests.
Production history examples do not cover redaction, encryption, or access controls.
The referenced resources/implementation-playbook.md file is not included.

use_cases.title: Create a First Workflow Test
use_cases.description: Build a fast pytest test around a Temporal workflow using time-skipping and clear assertions.
use_cases.target_user: Python developers new to Temporal testing

use_cases.title: Test Failure and Recovery Paths
use_cases.description: Mock activities and inject retryable or permanent failures to verify workflow behavior.

use_cases.title: Validate Changes Before Deployment
use_cases.description: Replay representative workflow histories in CI to detect non-deterministic code changes.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Workflow Test
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a pytest test for my Temporal Python workflow. Use time-skipping and explain the required fixture, worker, execution, and assertions.

prompt_templates.title: Activity Unit Tests
prompt_templates.prompt: Design ActivityEnvironment tests for these activities: [activities]. Cover normal results, invalid inputs, exceptions, and activity context behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Mocked Integration Suite
prompt_templates.prompt: Build an integration test plan for [workflow]. Mock these external activities: [activities]. Include retries, permanent failures, signals, queries, and parallel branches.

prompt_templates.title: Replay and CI Strategy
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a replay testing strategy for [workflow versions]. Include secure history handling, representative selection, deterministic checks, CI gates, retention, and failure diagnosis.

output_examples.input: How should I test a workflow with a thirty-day timer?
output_examples.output: Use a time-skipping WorkflowEnvironment, execute the workflow through a worker, and assert the final result without waiting for real time.

output_examples.input: Plan tests for a payment workflow with retrying activities.
output: Inject transient failures and verify the expected attempt count.
Inject a permanent validation failure and verify compensation.
Mock every external payment and inventory dependency.

output_examples.input: How can CI detect a non-deterministic workflow change?
output_examples.output: Replay protected, representative histories with the new workflow code. Fail the deployment check when replay reports a command sequence mismatch.

best_practices: Use time-skipping for workflow timers and keep tests independent.
Mock external dependencies while testing workflow orchestration and failure handling.
Protect production histories and replay representative versions before deployment.
anti_patterns: Do not call live external APIs from workflow tests.
Do not use wall-clock time or standard random generators inside workflows.
Do not store production histories in repositories or unrestricted CI artifacts.

faq.question: Does this skill run my tests?
faq.answer: No. It provides patterns and guidance that you apply and verify in your own environment.

faq.question: Which Temporal testing tools does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers WorkflowEnvironment, ActivityEnvironment, Worker, Replayer, pytest, Docker Compose, and coverage tools.

faq.question: Can it test long workflow timers quickly?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance uses time-skipping environments so long workflow timers complete without real delays.

faq.question: Does it cover mocked activities?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes static and dynamic mocks, retry failures, permanent errors, and multi-activity patterns.

faq.question: Can I use it for deployment checks?
faq.answer: Yes. It outlines replay tests and CI patterns for detecting non-deterministic workflow changes before deployment.

faq.question: How should I handle production histories?
faq.answer: Treat them as sensitive data. Apply redaction, encryption, strict access controls, limited retention, and restricted artifact handling.
